h1: Kacha Resort & Spa, Koh Chang — a beachfront resort on White Sand Beach that nailed a spot right in the middle of the beach
intro: White Sand Beach is the liveliest and most accessible beach on Koh Chang, and Kacha Resort & Spa sits right in the middle of it — a few steps out of your room and you're on the sand, and come evening you can stroll along the beach to restaurants, bars and the night market with ease · This is a big 4-star family resort with 206 rooms in 12 types, straddling the road as a sand-side zone (Seaside) and a hill-view zone (Hillside) · What a lot of people bring up is the 2 pools with a slide and a kids' pool, plus a location that walks to everything on White Sand Beach · Scored 9.3 from 174 reviews on Trip.com · Rooms start around THB 2,400/night at regular rates

body.html: Who Kacha Resort suits — to put it as simply as possible, Kacha Resort & Spa is a beachfront family resort for people who want to stay "in the middle of White Sand Beach" in a way that genuinely walks to everything · It isn't a quiet luxury resort that tucks you away at the far end of the island, and it isn't a small boutique selling privacy · It's a big 4-star resort sitting right in the middle of White Sand Beach — the busiest beach, lined end to end with restaurants, bars, convenience stores and a night market · The resort has been open for about 20 years, so it has the feel of a classic resort that's been updated bit by bit, with up to 12 room types and more than 206 rooms in total · Real reviews line up on who fits here: families bringing young kids to play in the pool and on the sand, couples who want a beachfront location on a manageable budget, and first-time visitors who don't want to risk staying further out · As for people chasing total peace and quiet, or a brand-new flawless resort, you may need to think twice, because this is a big resort in an area that's lively all day · The strength that's kept Kacha going this long is pairing a mid-beach location with an accessible price, a mix Thai and international families have kept choosing for years

Location and getting there — this is Kacha's number-one selling point · The resort is in the middle of White Sand Beach (Haad Sai Khao), the first beach most travelers think of when Koh Chang comes up · Unlike resorts at the head or far end of the beach, being in the middle means you can walk along the shore in both directions — the seafront restaurants, bars, massage shops, convenience stores and motorbike-rental spots are all a few minutes' walk away · On getting there: Koh Chang means taking a ferry across from the mainland piers (Ao Thammachat / Centerpoint), and from the pier to White Sand Beach is about a 15–20 min ride by songthaew or transfer · If you're driving, you can take the car onto the ferry · One thing worth knowing is that the resort itself straddles the island's main road, with a sea-side zone on one side and a hill zone on the other — Hillside guests have to cross the road (there's a crossing point) to get down to the beach, which is convenient but does have traffic passing, so keep a close eye on young kids · Another thing reviews mention is that the water in front is fairly shallow, and you have to wade out a way before it's deep enough for a proper swim — which is actually a plus for families with little ones

"Loved being right in the middle of the beach — turn left or right out of the resort and it's full of restaurants and massage shops, didn't need to call a ride once the whole trip · The kids played in the pool all day and wouldn't get out, and the beach in front is shallow so you can relax watching them"

Room types and decor — Kacha has up to 12 room types and more than 206 rooms in total, split into two big zones by side of the road · The Hillside zone (hill side) starts with the 40 sqm Deluxe Building Room, moving up to the 80 sqm Family Suite, 95 sqm Junior Suite and 110 sqm Grand Suite — many reviews call this zone's rooms "newer and fresher" since it was renovated later, and some higher-floor rooms get hill views with a partial glimpse of the sea · The Seaside zone (on the sand) runs from the 40 sqm Seaside Deluxe, the 40–50 sqm Deluxe Chalet and Deluxe Villa (standalone cottages with a garden terrace), the 50 sqm Beachfront Chalet closest to the sand, up to the Seaview Deluxe Villa and the largest room of all, the Pool Villa Suite, which stretches to 150–220 sqm with a private pool · The decor is tropical-resort style in wood and earth tones · Every room has a flat-screen TV, minibar, safe, air conditioning and free Wi-Fi · The honest point from reviews is that room standards aren't consistent across every building, because the resort has been open for about 20 years — some rooms in the older zone are starting to show their age, while the renovated rooms look much fresher · Many reviews suggest asking to see the room first, or specifying clearly at booking that you want a recently renovated one · On the praise side, the beds are comfortable, the rooms are bigger than the price suggests, and the standalone villas give good privacy

Facilities and pools — Kacha's highlight is its pools and family activities · The resort has 2 pools — the beachfront pool near the sea, and a larger one in the Hillside zone with a separate kids' pool and a slide, giving the kids a fun place to play · Both pools have a swim-up bar so you can order drinks in the water · There's also a Thai-massage spa and treatments, fitness, kids' club, library and internet room, and a meeting room · Plus transfer service and island tours, bike rental and water activities · To be straight about it, reviews note that the poolside loungers sometimes run out at peak times, so if you want a good spot, head down early · The beachfront pool is fairly small and crowded in high season, while the hill-zone pool is bigger and quieter · Some fitness equipment is getting old per reviews, but it's enough for a light workout · Overall, for family activities Kacha does well at this price point

Food and bars — the resort's main restaurant is the beachfront Kacha Restaurant, serving from breakfast through dinner with a sea view right in front · Plenty of reviews praise the breakfast buffet for its variety and the sea view while you eat, with both Thai and Western dishes to choose from · There's the Hinoiri Bar and a poolside bar for evening drinks, plus a coffee shop for coffee and snacks · The honest point is that many reviews say food and drinks at the resort are fairly pricey compared with places outside it · But that's barely an issue, because the mid-beach location on White Sand Beach means a few minutes' walk gets you to seafront restaurants, seafood spots and budget-friendly Thai eateries lining the whole beach · So a lot of people have breakfast at the resort and head out for other meals — one of the upsides of staying on such a lively beach · The beachfront bar at sunset is also a chill spot that reviews bring up often

Service — staff is where Kacha earns steady praise in real reviews · Many say the staff are friendly, smiling, polite and helpful, especially the front-desk and poolside teams · Arranging tours, calling rides and recommending places around the island all run smoothly · For a big 206-room resort with lots of family guests, keeping that warm kind of care is a real strength · To be fair, some reviews note that responses can slow down at times when the resort is full, and that cleaning standards in spots like the pool edge could still improve · But on the whole, service stays a positive that brings many guests back

What real reviews say (both praise and gripes) — pulling from Trip.com, Booking.com and Tripadvisor, the picture is fairly consistent · On the praise side: a mid-beach location on White Sand Beach that walks to everything, a varied breakfast with a sea view, friendly and attentive staff, a pool and slide the kids love, a shallow beach in front that suits families, and good value for the price relative to the location · On the watch-outs: the most-mentioned is the resort's roughly 20-year age, which leaves some rooms and common areas looking dated and due for a renovation · After that: pricey food and drinks at the resort, not enough poolside loungers at peak times, shallow water in front that means a long wade before you can swim, a pool edge that could be cleaned better at times, and some mosquitoes in the sand-side rooms · Most of these gripes can be handled by picking your room (ask for a renovated one) and setting the right expectation — that this is a lively mid-beach family resort, not a brand-new, quiet boutique

"The staff were lovely and breakfast with a sea view was a treat · but the room we got at first looked a bit dated, so we asked to move to a recently renovated hill-zone room — much fresher. Next time I'll specify it right at booking"

Price comparison and value — starting rates for a Hillside Deluxe run around THB 2,400–2,800/night at regular rates, with low-season deals that can drop to the low THB 2,000s · Sand-side rooms and standalone villas sit roughly in the THB 3,500–6,000+ range depending on size and timing, while the Pool Villa Suite is the resort's top price bracket · Compared with other White Sand Beach resorts, Kacha sits in the accessible 4-star group selling a mid-beach location — cheaper than the far-end luxury resorts like The Dewa or Emerald Cove, but far easier for walking around · If the heart of your trip is bringing the family to play in the pool and on the sand, then walking out to eat and explore White Sand Beach every day without calling a ride, the money you put toward this location pays off · But if you'll pay more for a brand-new room and quiet, look at a newer-built resort instead

Good to know before booking — a few things make the stay smoother · One, specify which zone you want — the Seaside zone walks to the sand fast but some rooms are older, while the Hillside zone has fresher rooms but you cross the road to reach the beach · Two, if room condition matters to you, ask for a recently renovated room at booking or check at check-in · Three, if you're bringing little kids, the shallow beach is a plus, but mind the road crossing between the two zones · Four, head down early to claim a poolside lounger in high season (November–April), because it gets crowded · Five, budget for meals out, since resort food costs more than the beachfront eateries · Six, Koh Chang in low season (May–October) gets a lot of rain and ferry schedules may change, so check the weather and book with free cancellation

Summary — from all the real reviews, Kacha Resort & Spa fits best for families and couples who want to stay on White Sand Beach, in the middle of it, on a manageable budget · A location that walks to restaurants, bars and the market every day, pools with a slide for the kids, a shallow safe beach out front, and friendly staff have kept it a popular pick on White Sand Beach for years · If you're after a flawless brand-new room in every corner, a quiet private resort, or you'd rather skip the buzz of a popular beach, this may not be the answer, and you should look at a far-end resort or a quieter beach like Klong Prao or Kai Bae instead · But for a family trip wanting the most convenient beachfront location on Koh Chang at an accessible price — Kacha answers that need neatly, and it's why it keeps getting booked again

faq.q: Where on Koh Chang is Kacha Resort, and what can you walk to?
faq.a: The resort is in the middle of White Sand Beach (Haad Sai Khao), the liveliest and most accessible beach on Koh Chang · You can stroll the shore in both directions to seafront restaurants, bars, massage shops, convenience stores and a night market within a few minutes' walk · From the ferry pier to the resort is about a 15–20 min drive

It's a great fit for families with young kids and couples who want to stay on White Sand Beach on a manageable budget · There's a pool with a slide and a kids' pool, a shallow safe beach in front, and beachfront strolling every day · If you're after quiet privacy or a brand-new room, a far-end resort or Klong Prao Beach may suit you better

faq.q: What's Kacha Resort's starting price, and what room types are there?
faq.a: Prices start around THB 2,400/night for a Hillside Deluxe at regular rates · There are up to 12 types, from a 40 sqm Deluxe, a 50 sqm Deluxe Villa and Beachfront Chalet, up to a 110 sqm Grand Suite and a 150–220 sqm Pool Villa Suite · High-season rates (Nov–Apr) go up, so compare several platforms before booking

faq.q: Are Kacha's rooms old, and which zone should you pick?
faq.a: The resort has been open for about 20 years, so room standards aren't consistent across every building · Many reviews say the Hillside zone (hill side) was renovated more recently and the rooms are fresher, while the Seaside zone (on the sand) walks to the beach faster but some rooms are starting to age · We'd suggest specifying clearly at booking that you want a recently renovated room

faq.q: Does Kacha Resort have a pool and activities for kids?
faq.a: There are 2 pools — a beachfront pool and a bigger hill-zone pool with a separate kids' pool and a slide, plus a swim-up bar · There's also a kids' club, Thai-massage spa, fitness, and a shallow beach in front that's safe for young kids · It's a family resort that reviews praise for its activities at this price point

faq.q: What's the food like at Kacha?
faq.a: The main restaurant is the beachfront Kacha Restaurant, serving from morning to evening · Reviews praise the breakfast buffet for its variety and sea view · There's the Hinoiri Bar and a poolside bar for the evening · The watch-out is that food and drinks at the resort are fairly pricey, but since it's in the middle of White Sand Beach, a few minutes' walk gets you to seafood spots and budget-friendly seafront restaurants
